## Options on a zero-coupon bond

The QuantLib R binding gives no direct price of this option. The baseline is the closed form of the legacy text, in R.

```{r}
#| label: option-inputs
legacy <- lagrange_objects(
  "part2_quantive_riemann/ch06_irs_calibration.qmd",
  c("compute_hw_bond_option_price_LRL", "hw_initial_zero_rate", "hw_reference_a", "hw_reference_sigma", "tbl_bond_option_market")
)
options_table <- legacy$tbl_bond_option_market |> select(option_maturity, bond_maturity, strike)
knitr::kable(options_table, digits = 4, caption = "Options")
curve_date <- "2026-11-02"
show_inputs(list(flat_zero_rate = legacy$hw_initial_zero_rate, mean_reversion = legacy$hw_reference_a, volatility = legacy$hw_reference_sigma, curve_date = curve_date))
```

```{r}
#| label: option-calls
baseline_options <- pmap_dbl(options_table, \(option_maturity, bond_maturity, strike) {
  legacy$compute_hw_bond_option_price_LRL(option_maturity, bond_maturity, strike, legacy$hw_reference_a, legacy$hw_reference_sigma, legacy$hw_initial_zero_rate)
})
option_curve <- flat_curve(curve_date, legacy$hw_initial_zero_rate)
riemann_options <- RiemannFinMath::hull_white_bond_option(
  "call", options_table$strike, options_table$option_maturity, options_table$bond_maturity,
  legacy$hw_reference_a, legacy$hw_reference_sigma, option_curve
)
```

```{r}
#| label: option-results
compare_values(
  sprintf("Option %.1fy on bond %.0fy", options_table$option_maturity, options_table$bond_maturity), "bp of a bond worth 1",
  1e4 * baseline_options, 1e4 * riemann_options, "R closed form"
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Swaptions

The legacy text describes the extension to swaptions without an example. These inputs use its parameters, on a notional of 100.

```{r}
#| label: swaption-inputs
swaption <- list(today = curve_date, start_days = 730L, years = 5L, fixed_rate = 0.03, nominal = 100, rate = legacy$hw_initial_zero_rate, a = legacy$hw_reference_a, sigma = legacy$hw_reference_sigma)
show_inputs(c(swaption, list(type = "payer", schedule = "annual, no calendar, Actual/365 (Fixed)")))
```

QuantLib:

```{r}
#| label: swaption-quantlib
dc <- QuantLib::Actual365Fixed()
ql_set_evaluation_date(swaption$today)
today <- ql_date(swaption$today)
start <- ql_date(as.Date(swaption$today) + swaption$start_days)
end <- ql_date(as.Date(swaption$today) + swaption$start_days + 365L * swaption$years)
handle <- QuantLib::YieldTermStructureHandle(QuantLib::FlatForward(today, swaption$rate, dc, "Continuous"))
schedule <- QuantLib::Schedule(start, end, QuantLib::Period("Annual"), QuantLib::NullCalendar(), "Unadjusted", "Unadjusted", "Backward", FALSE)
index <- QuantLib::IborIndex("Synthetic1Y", QuantLib::Period("Annual"), 0L, QuantLib::JPYCurrency(), QuantLib::NullCalendar(), "Unadjusted", FALSE, dc, handle)
ql_swap <- QuantLib::VanillaSwap(QuantLib::Swap_Payer_get(), swaption$nominal, schedule, swaption$fixed_rate, dc, schedule, index, 0, dc)
ql_european <- function(a, sigma) {
  option <- QuantLib::Swaption(ql_swap, QuantLib::EuropeanExercise(start))
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(option, QuantLib::JamshidianSwaptionEngine(QuantLib::HullWhite(handle, a, sigma)))
  option$NPV()
}
schedule_serials <- map_int(seq_len(QuantLib::Schedule_size(schedule)) - 1L, \(i) {
  as.integer(QuantLib::Date_serialNumber(QuantLib::Schedule_date(schedule, i)))
})
exercise_dates <- do.call(QuantLib::DateVector, list())
walk(head(schedule_serials, -1), \(s) QuantLib::DateVector_push_back(exercise_dates, QuantLib::Date(s)))
ql_bermudan <- function(steps) {
  option <- QuantLib::Swaption(ql_swap, QuantLib::BermudanExercise(exercise_dates))
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(option, QuantLib::TreeSwaptionEngine(QuantLib::HullWhite(handle, swaption$a, swaption$sigma), steps))
  option$NPV()
}
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: swaption-riemann
days <- schedule_serials - as.integer(QuantLib::Date_serialNumber(today))
times <- days / 365
payment_times <- times[-1]
coupons <- swaption$nominal * swaption$fixed_rate * diff(times) # amounts, not rates
riemann_curve <- flat_curve(swaption$today, swaption$rate)
riemann_european <- RiemannFinMath::hull_white_swaption(TRUE, times[1], payment_times, coupons, swaption$a, swaption$sigma, riemann_curve, nominal = swaption$nominal)
riemann_bermudan <- RiemannFinMath::hull_white_bermudan_swaption(TRUE, times[1], payment_times, coupons, head(times, -1), swaption$a, swaption$sigma, riemann_curve, nominal = swaption$nominal)
```

```{r}
#| label: swaption-results
h <- 1e-6
tree <- map_dbl(c(500L, 1000L, 2000L), ql_bermudan)
bind_rows(
  compare_values("European value", "per 100", ql_european(swaption$a, swaption$sigma), riemann_european$value),
  compare_values(
    "European, derivative in mean reversion", "per 100, per percent",
    (ql_european(swaption$a + h, swaption$sigma) - ql_european(swaption$a - h, swaption$sigma)) / (2 * h) * 0.01,
    riemann_european$d_mean_reversion * 0.01, "QuantLib, finite difference"
  ),
  compare_values(
    "European, derivative in volatility", "per 100, per percent",
    (ql_european(swaption$a, swaption$sigma + h) - ql_european(swaption$a, swaption$sigma - h)) / (2 * h) * 0.01,
    riemann_european$d_volatility * 0.01, "QuantLib, finite difference"
  ),
  compare_values("Bermudan value, tree of 1000 steps", "per 100", tree[2], riemann_bermudan),
  compare_values("Bermudan value, tree of 2000 steps", "per 100", tree[3], riemann_bermudan),
  not_comparable("Bermudan: the tree from 500 to 1000 steps", "per 100", tree[1], tree[2], "The tree against itself: how far the baseline still moves", "QuantLib tree itself"),
  not_comparable("Bermudan: the tree from 1000 to 2000 steps", "per 100", tree[2], tree[3], "The tree against itself: how far the baseline still moves", "QuantLib tree itself")
) |>
  show_results()
```

The Bermudan methods are different: QuantLib rolls back on a trinomial tree, and RiemannFinMath takes an exact conditional expectation on a state grid at each step. A FAIL in these rows is a numerical difference between two methods. The rows on the tree against itself show how much of it is the tree's own convergence error.

## Callable bond

QuantLib has a callable bond on a tree, but it is a different calculation from the legacy text. The baseline is the legacy text's own R function, with the same state grid and quadrature.

```{r}
#| label: callable-inputs
callable <- lagrange_objects(
  "part2_quantive_riemann/ch08_early_redemption_models.qmd",
  c("notional", "coupon_rate", "period_years", "maturity_years", "flat_zero_rate", "first_call_year", "call_price", "tbl_cashflows",
    "compute_normal_quadrature_LRL", "compute_hw_shift_integral_LRL", "compute_discounted_step_LRL", "compute_callable_bond_LRL")
)
show_inputs(list(
  notional = callable$notional, coupon_rate = callable$coupon_rate, period_years = callable$period_years, maturity_years = callable$maturity_years,
  flat_zero_rate = callable$flat_zero_rate, first_call_year = callable$first_call_year, call_price = callable$call_price,
  mean_reversion = 0.15, volatility = 0.012
))
```

```{r}
#| label: callable-calls
flows <- callable$tbl_cashflows
baseline_callable <- function(volatility, points = 321L, nodes = 24L) {
  callable$compute_callable_bond_LRL(
    flows, flat_rate = callable$flat_zero_rate, mean_reversion = 0.15, volatility = volatility,
    number_of_grid_points = points, grid_limit = 0.13, quadrature_nodes = nodes
  )
}
callable_curve <- flat_curve(curve_date, callable$flat_zero_rate)
riemann_callable <- function(volatility, points = 321L, nodes = 24L) {
  RiemannFinMath::hull_white_callable_bond(
    flows$payment_time, flows$coupon, flows$principal_at_maturity, flows$call_principal,
    0.15, volatility, callable_curve, points = points, limit = 0.13, nodes = nodes
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: callable-results
base_b <- baseline_callable(0.012)
base_r <- riemann_callable(0.012)
scenarios <- tibble(volatility = c(0.006, 0.02))
grids <- tibble(points = c(161L, 641L), nodes = c(16L, 32L))
bind_rows(
  compare_values("Bullet", "per 100", base_b$bullet_price, base_r$bullet, "Legacy R function"),
  compare_values("Callable", "per 100", base_b$callable_price, base_r$callable, "Legacy R function"),
  compare_values("Value of the issuer's call", "per 100", base_b$issuer_call_value, base_r$issuer_call_value, "Legacy R function"),
  compare_values(
    sprintf("Callable, volatility %.3f", scenarios$volatility), "per 100",
    map_dbl(scenarios$volatility, \(v) baseline_callable(v)$callable_price),
    map_dbl(scenarios$volatility, \(v) riemann_callable(v)$callable), "Legacy R function"
  ),
  compare_values(
    sprintf("Callable, grid %d, nodes %d", grids$points, grids$nodes), "per 100",
    map2_dbl(grids$points, grids$nodes, \(p, n) baseline_callable(0.012, p, n)$callable_price),
    map2_dbl(grids$points, grids$nodes, \(p, n) riemann_callable(0.012, p, n)$callable), "Legacy R function"
  )
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Not available

Hull-White calibration, the exercise decisions of the callable bond, the simulated short-rate paths, HJM, BGM/LMM, FMM and MBS are in the legacy text and not in RiemannFinMath. See @sec-gaps.

## Differences of wrapper and core

```{r}
#| label: design
tribble(
  ~Layer,    ~Aspect,        ~QuantLib,                                                ~RiemannFinMath,
  "Wrapper", "Swap",         "`Schedule`, an index, a `VanillaSwap`, an exercise, an engine", "Times and coupons as vectors",
  "Wrapper", "Dates",        "Dates through the curve's day counter",                  "Times in years from the curve's date",
  "Wrapper", "Fixed leg",    "A rate and a day counter",                               "Coupon amounts, in the units of the notional",
  "Core",    "European",     "Jamshidian; searches `r*` to 1e-8",                      "Jamshidian; searches to 1e-12 and refines by Newton",
  "Core",    "Bermudan",     "Trinomial tree; converges with the steps",               "Exact conditional expectation on a state grid",
  "Core",    "Model values", "The model holds its parameters and observes the curve",  "Parameters are arguments; no model object",
  "Core",    "Derivatives",  "Not exposed",                                            "Automatic differentiation for the European swaption"
) |>
  show_design()
```
